synopsis: ASAM OpenODD 1.0.0, released on 3 April 2025, provides a technology-independent operating-domain data model in machine-readable YAML and CSV, with restrictive definitions specifying what is allowed and permissive definitions specifying what is excluded [f6707, f6708, f13246]. Its normative scope is automated road vehicles, with default attributes dominated by lanes and junctions; its structure is transferable to off-road validation, but its content is not directly transferable [f6709, f6642, f13245]. Operating-domain definitions establish testing boundaries and therefore the meaning of coverage, making an appropriate taxonomy foundational to validation [f6782]. OpenODD is assessed as having moderate off-road fit, and the manufacturer or industry must author and govern an off-road taxonomy; the proposed adaptation combines on-road and off-road patterns, but its arrangement remains expert opinion [f7162, f7163, f6714]. The booklet recommends a manufacturer-owned, domain-neutral, version-controlled scenario catalog using Scenic or an in-house YAML schema with an OpenODD-style taxonomy, exporting to OpenSCENARIO where tools require it [f14491, f7198].
